::: {.content}

My research sits at the intersection of geospatial artificial intelligence and ecology, developing computational methods to understand how forests and landscapes change and what those changes mean for the planet.

## Research Areas

::: {.card-grid}

::: {.card-item}
[🛰️]{.card-icon}
### Forest Disturbance Mapping
Automated detection of deforestation, degradation, and recovery using satellite time series and machine learning classifiers.

[Change Detection]{.card-tag} [Landsat]{.card-tag} [Sentinel]{.card-tag}
:::

::: {.card-item}
[🌍]{.card-icon}
### Landscape Connectivity
Modeling how landscape structure and fragmentation affect species movement, gene flow, and ecosystem resilience.

[Connectivity]{.card-tag} [Graph Theory]{.card-tag}
:::

::: {.card-item}
[📊]{.card-icon}
### Spatial Modeling
Developing geospatial machine learning models for ecological prediction, including species distribution models and biomass estimation.

[GeoAI]{.card-tag} [Prediction]{.card-tag}
:::

::: {.card-item}
[🌿]{.card-icon}
### Biodiversity Assessment
Using multi-sensor remote sensing to characterize habitats and predict biodiversity patterns across spatial scales.

[Biodiversity]{.card-tag} [LiDAR]{.card-tag}
:::

:::
